acceptance.criterion_verbatim: THE POSITIVE CONTROL FIRED, AS A SEPARATE INVOCATION: for each role, at least one action it must NOT have, simulated separately, returning a deny. If every simulation in the instance returns `allowed`, this criterion FAILS regardless of the other results -- an instrument that cannot say no has not said yes.
acceptance.invocation: Each control is its own aws iam simulate-principal-policy invocation, never batched with a target -- a control batched with its target is corrupted by its own presence.
acceptance.output_evidence: 17 of 45 simulations returned a DENY, so the instrument demonstrably says no and the 28 allowed results are load-bearing. PER ROLE, at least one control each: RECONCILER -- dynamodb:PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem on the table all explicitDeny (matched its own Deny statement), and ses:SendEmail implicitDeny (no grant at all). CLI -- wafv2:UpdateIPSet explicitDeny on all four sets, dynamodb:DeleteItem implicitDeny, s3:PutObject on the evidence bucket implicitDeny. SENTINEL -- wafv2:UpdateIPSet explicitDeny on all four sets, dynamodb:DeleteItem implicitDeny, s3:PutObject outside the two granted prefixes implicitDeny. TWO DISTINCT DENY KINDS OBSERVED AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS: explicitDeny comes from a written Deny statement and is unambiguous; implicitDeny means merely no matching Allow and is a NAMED FALSE-DENY MODE of this instrument -- it is byte-identical to what a typo'd action name or an unsatisfied condition returns. The explicit Deny statements the owning seats built therefore make this criterion sharper, not just the policies safer.
acceptance.denominator: 17 denies of 45 total simulations; 3 of 3 roles carry at least one control; controls per role: reconciler 4, CLI 6, sentinel 6

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: C-2 AND C-11 ARE VERDICTED EXPLICITLY, NOT INFERRED: the reconciler ALLOWED `wafv2:UpdateIPSet` on ALL FOUR SETS, one simulation per set; the CLI and the sentinel DENIED the same action on the same resources, each as its own simulation. This is the invariant the whole chain rests on and it gets its own named result. THE DENOMINATOR IS 4 OF 4 AND IT IS PRINTED, OR THIS CRITERION FAILS.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: CONDITIONS WERE EVALUATED WITH CONTEXT, AND THE LENS'S LIMITS ARE STATED: for any conditioned statement, the `--context-entries` supplied and why. Plus an explicit sentence naming what this verdict does NOT cover -- resource policies, SCPs, permission boundaries -- so a later reader does not read it as wider than it is. `comp-iam` output, if run, is labelled DESIRED-plane and is never cited as an ALLOW.
acceptance.invocation: aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn <sentinel> --action-names ses:SendEmail --resource-arns arn:aws:ses:us-east-1:313476888478:identity/opalinvest.dev --context-entries ContextKeyName=ses:FromAddress,ContextKeyValues=noreply@opalinvest.dev,ContextKeyType=string -- and the SAME call again with the context entry omitted
acceptance.output_evidence: ONE CONDITIONED STATEMENT IN THE ENTIRE CHAIN, 1 of 1, established by reading all three policies at source rather than by sampling: the sentinel's ses:SendEmail, conditioned StringEquals ses:FromAddress = noreply@opalinvest.dev. THE TRAP WAS DEMONSTRATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, NOT ASSERTED: WITH the context entry -> allowed, matching role_opal-sentinel_opal-sentinel-table-evidence-and-notify. WITHOUT it -> implicitDeny, matched statements empty. That implicitDeny is byte-identical to the one a missing grant produces, so without the context entry this face would have filed a FALSE DENY on a correctly-granted permission -- an UNDER-permissioning verdict, which sends a seat to widen a policy that was already right, and which would have looked like diligence. The warning was written into iam_sentinel.tf by 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~S addressed to this face; it was correct and load-bearing. WHAT THIS VERDICT DOES NOT COVER, stated so it is not read wider than it is: (1) RESOURCE POLICIES -- the opal-security-evidence bucket policy and the CMK key policy. Concretely relevant here: the CMK's AllowViaDynamoDBAndS3InThisAccountOnly is conditioned on kms:ViaService for dynamodb and s3 ONLY, so a role calling KMS DIRECTLY sits outside it and an identity-policy 'allowed' for kms:Decrypt could still fail in production; all three roles were built to reach KMS only through the services, which is why this does not bite. (2) SCPs, permission boundaries and session policies. (3) WHETHER THE CODE MAKES THE CALL -- an allowed pair is not an exercised pair, and the Lambda function code does not exist yet. (4) C-2's EXCLUSIVITY: this face verdicted THREE principals, while C-2 claims nothing else in the account ever calls UpdateIPSet -- a claim over 221 roles plus users and resource-policy paths. A fourth principal holding that permission would leave all 45 results unchanged. That enumeration is S15-AC3's criterion and is NOT discharged here. comp-iam: NOT RUN, and DECLARED-NOT-APPLICABLE per the face's own preflight -- it is a DESIRED-plane lens over Terraform, the PRD records at s.4 that it does not parse the Deny statements it reports, and this whole verdict turns on Deny statements. Its silence is never an ALLOW and it is cited nowhere in this instance.
acceptance.denominator: 1 of 1 conditioned statements identified across all three policies and simulated both with and without context; 4 categories of non-coverage named explicitly

mutant.description: S22-AC2 IS the planted mutant and the face wrote it to be able to fail: an instance in which every simulation returns allowed FAILS on its face, because an instrument that cannot say no has not said yes. Beyond that, each MUST-NOT pair is itself a mutation of the corresponding MUST-HAVE claim -- the same action, the same instrument, a principal that should NOT hold it. The sharpest is wafv2:UpdateIPSet run against all three roles on the identical four ARNs: if the instrument were returning a constant, the reconciler and the sentinel could not disagree on the same call.
mutant.expected: The reconciler allowed on all four sets; the sentinel and the CLI denied on those same four. If all three returned allowed, C-2 is not enforced and the verdict is void; if all three returned deny, the instrument is broken and the allowed results mean nothing.
mutant.observed: Reconciler allowed x4; sentinel explicitDeny x4; CLI explicitDeny x4 -- the same action on the same resources, splitting by principal exactly as the policies declare. Fleet-wide, 28 allowed and 17 denied over 45 simulations. The instrument discriminates by principal, by resource prefix (sentinel s3:PutObject allowed under cases/ and reports/daily/, implicitDeny under waf-logs/) and by CONDITION (ses:SendEmail allowed with the context entry, implicitDeny without it, same call otherwise).

determinism.method: The entire 45-simulation suite was run twice against the same applied roles and the two outputs compared; the second run is the committed artifact.
determinism.observed: Run 1 and run 2 identical: 45 simulations, 28 allowed, 17 denied, 0 mismatches, 44 OK-flagged rows plus the one deliberately-unflagged trap-demonstration row in both.

declared_exclusions.item: C-2's EXCLUSIVITY over the account is not established.
declared_exclusions.reason: This face verdicted 3 principals. C-2 claims nothing else in the account ever calls wafv2:UpdateIPSet -- a claim over 221 roles plus users and resource-policy paths. A fourth principal holding it would leave all 45 results unchanged. That enumeration is S15-AC3's criterion, explicitly a read-dependency of this cell and not claimed by it. Named rather than left to inference, because a scoped check reading as a population check is the shape that has bitten this project three times tonight.

declared_exclusions.item: Resource policies, SCPs, permission boundaries and session policies were not evaluated.
declared_exclusions.reason: simulate-principal-policy does not evaluate them. Concretely relevant: the CMK's key policy is conditioned on kms:ViaService for dynamodb and s3 only, so an identity-policy allowed for kms:Decrypt would not imply a direct KMS call succeeds. All three roles were built to reach KMS only through the services, so it does not bite -- but the verdict does not prove that, the policy reading does.

declared_exclusions.item: Whether the code makes these calls at all.
declared_exclusions.reason: The Lambda function code for all three roles does not exist yet. An allowed pair is not an exercised pair, and an over-permissioned role is only visible once both the policy and the code exist. This verdict certifies the grant matches the DECLARED need.

declared_exclusions.item: The CLI's trust-policy breadth was not adjudicated.
declared_exclusions.reason: Its trust names one principal, following opal-security-admin's ruled pattern. Whether the unblock CLI should be assumable by a wider operator set is flagged by its own carrier as 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z's call. Named so the verdict does not read a deliberately narrow trust as an oversight.

DECLARED-NOT-APPLICABLE per the face's own preflight and its binding clause. It is a DESIRED-plane lens over Terraform; the PRD records at s.4 that it does not parse the Deny statements it reports, and this verdict turns on Deny statements. Its silence is never an ALLOW, so running it would have added no evidence this instance relies on.
